commands.name: openspec-propose
commands.description: Propose a new OpenSpec change with all artifacts generated in one step. Use when the user wants to quickly describe what they want to build and get a complete proposal with design, specs, and tasks ready for implementation. Also use when the user says "openspec propose" or "opsx propose". (managed)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

# The gate after the fresh review of round 3: round 4, 1 November

Input: the fresh review of e16's round 3 (`runs/20261101-053638-claude-opus-5-5`). Its R1 is a BLOCK whose fix needs a decision; Prem answered it, and answered the dependency question raised after round 3. Under the stop rule in the plan, R1 goes back to the author and a fresh review checks the fix. The review's R2, R3 and R4 need no decision and go to the coding agent in e17 as extra tasks.

## Decisions

| # | Question | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| G7 | R1: on MySQL the old code cannot start against the migrated table, because the old `db/mysql/data.sql` inserts pets by position and runs at every start. How does MySQL move from the old code to the new? | **Two releases.** Release 1 ships only the column lists for the pet inserts in `data.sql` (H2 and MySQL); they work on the old table and on the migrated one. Then the migration script runs. Then release 2 ships the microchip number. Rollback from release 2 redeploys release 1, which works on the migrated table. Amend D23: its premise "the old code keeps working against the new table because it never names the column" is false on MySQL while the old `data.sql` inserts by position; it holds from release 1 on. Record G7 as a new decision that amends D23; do not delete D23's text, mark what G7 changes. The change stays one OpenSpec change; the two releases are ordered steps in the design's deployment plan and in the tasks |
| G8 | Task 1.5 adds `org.testcontainers:testcontainers-postgresql` for the Postgres migration test. Add the dependency? | **No.** Adding a dependency stays with a person, and this one is not needed: `PostgresIntegrationTests` starts Postgres through Spring Boot's Docker Compose support, already in the pom, and the MySQL tests use the `testcontainers-mysql` already there. The migration tests follow those existing patterns and add no dependency |

Why D23's premise was wrong (for the log): the round-3 gate file stated it, and nobody checked it against the old `data.sql`. The positional seed inserts are the same root cause as the `data.sql` BLOCK of the first reviews.

## Fixes that need no decision

None in this round. R2, R3 and R4 of the review go to e17.

## Left as they are

- R5 to R8 of the review: informational.

content.content:
1	I found one blocking problem: the migration plan's rollback fails on MySQL. There are also three test or spec gaps a person can fix mechanically, and four informational notes. `openspec validate pc-301 --strict` reports `Change 'pc-301' is valid`, but that only checks the format, not the meaning. I couldn't use Docker (the Bash call was denied), so nothing about MySQL or Postgres behaviour was run. Those claims are labelled INFERRED.
2	
3	## 1. Decisions
4	
5	| Decision | Verdict | Where |
6	|---|---|---|
7	| D1 term | CARRIED | Proposal, design, spec and tasks avoid "chip number", "chip ID" and "transponder" (whole-word grep: only hits are in `decisions.md:7,9,34`, where D1 names the banned words and "chips" means the devices) |
8	| D2 optional | CARRIED | spec "Microchip number is optional"; task 2.1 |
9	| D3 15 digits, ISO only | CARRIED | spec "exactly 15 digits", scenario "A 10-character non-ISO number is rejected" |
10	| D4 unique across owners | CARRIED | spec "unique across all pets", scenario "A number held by another owner's pet" |
11	| D5 no lookup | CARRIED | proposal:5,19; design Non-Goals |
12	| D6 owner's page | CARRIED | `specs/owner-details/spec.md`; task 5.1 |
13	| D7 change number | CARRIED | spec "A pet's microchip number can be changed" |
14	| D8 empty clears, form shows stored | CARRIED | spec "Clearing…" and "The edit form shows the stored microchip number"; design 6 |
15	| D9 trim, remove spaces | CARRIED | spec "stored as its digits"; design 2 |
16	| D10 messages | CARRIED | design 3, design 4; spec scenarios |
17	| D11 no details of the other pet | CARRIED | spec "unique across all pets"; task 3.4 |
18	| D12 named constraint on 3 DBs | CARRIED | design 5 (on Postgres it is a unique index, as D23 allows) |
19	| D13 MySQL name constraint not fixed | CARRIED | design Non-Goals |
20	| D14 own number | CARRIED | spec "A pet keeps its own microchip number"; design 4 (two queries) |
21	| D15 no prefix check | CARRIED | design 3 |
22	| D16 empty value under the label | CARRIED | owner-details scenario "A pet without a microchip number" |
23	| D17 one error per field, reported with the others | CARRIED | spec "One microchip number error at a time"; MODIFIED "Validation errors are reported together" |
24	| D18 placement is a design call | CARRIED | design 4 |
25	| D19 validator method called from `catch` | CARRIED | design 5; tasks 4.1, 4.3 |
26	| D20 | Replaced by D23 | — |
27	| D21 H2 add/edit/clear test | CARRIED | task 3.5 |
28	| D22 accepted wrong-pet case | CARRIED | proposal:23; design Risks |
29	| D23 migration | CARRIED in text, but its premise is wrong on MySQL | design 8. D23 says "the old code keeps working against the new table because it never names the column". On MySQL that is false (R1). |
30	| D24 no visit form | CARRIED | design Non-Goals; tasks follow-up |
31	
32	**Added scope:** none that isn't needed.
33	- The `owner-details` capability (D6), the message keys (the sync test requires them), the `data.sql` column lists (positional inserts) and the `testcontainers-postgresql` dependency (D23's tests) all follow from a decision or the code.
34	- The seed-insert fix is correct for new databases (VERIFIED: `db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48` insert by position; `db/postgres/data.sql:36-48` names its columns).
35	
36	**Open section:** "None on PC-301's frontier". The follow-ups are listed in tasks.md (Workflow follow-up). The ticket raises no question that the log and the change leave unanswered: the "scanned" use is D5, "two pets" is D4, and there is no pet deletion (VERIFIED: grep for `delete|remove` in `owner/` finds nothing).
37	
38	## 2. Findings
39	
40	**R1: BLOCK.** Where: design Decision 8, "Rollback" step 1 and "Deployment" step 1; D23.
41	- **Claim:** On MySQL, the old code cannot start against a migrated `pets` table. The old `data.sql` inserts pets by position with 5 values, the migrated table has 6 columns, and init runs on every start with no `continue-on-error`. So "redeploy the old code" (rollback) fails, and so does any restart of old instances between step 1 and step 2. Postgres is not affected.
42	- **Evidence:**
43	  - VERIFIED: `db/mysql/data.sql:36` `INSERT IGNORE INTO pets VALUES (1, 'Leo', '2000-09-07', 1, 1);`
44	  - VERIFIED: `application-mysql.properties:7` `spring.sql.init.mode=always`. No `spring.sql.init.continue-on-error` in that file or in `application.properties`.
45	  - VERIFIED: design:114 says "The old code keeps working against the new table because it never names the column".
46	  - VERIFIED: Postgres's old `data.sql` names its columns (`db/postgres/data.sql:36`).
47	  - INFERRED, not run: MySQL raises error 1136, "Column count doesn't match value count", and `IGNORE` does not suppress it. That would make startup fail.
48	- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if MySQL 9.7 accepts a 5-value positional `INSERT IGNORE` into a 6-column table, or if something else sets `continue-on-error=true`.
49	- **Confidence:** medium-high.
50	
51	**R2: AUTO-FIX+REVERIFY.** Where: task 1.5.
52	- **Claim:** The migration test runs the *new* `schema.sql` on the migrated database, but never the *old* `schema.sql` and `data.sql`. So nothing checks D23's "old code keeps working" claim, the very assumption R1 breaks.
53	- **Evidence:** tasks.md:11, "Finally it runs the new `schema.sql` against the migrated database". There is no step for the old scripts.
54	- **Fix:** After migrating, run the old commit's `schema.sql` and `data.sql` too, and assert they succeed.
55	- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if some other task runs the old init scripts against a migrated table.
56	- **Confidence:** high.
57	
58	**R3: AUTO-FIX+REVERIFY.** Where: design Decision 4; task 2.1.
59	- **Claim:** The design doesn't say the uniqueness query is skipped when there is no number. A Spring Data derived `existsByMicrochipNumber(null)` turns into `IS NULL`, so it would find any pet without a number and reject a second pet without one as a duplicate.
60	- **Why tests could miss it:** Task 2.1's "no number accepted" uses a mocked repository, which returns `false` by default, so that test would pass with the bug. Indirect coverage exists: all seeded H2 pets have no number, so task 3.5's clear step and the existing `PetClinicConcurrencyTests` would probably fail. That coverage is accidental, not designed.
61	- **Evidence:**
62	  - VERIFIED: design:55 says "runs only when the format check passes". It doesn't say whether an absent number "passes".
63	  - INFERRED: Spring Data JPA turns a null argument into `IS NULL`.
64	- **Fix:** In design 4, state that the query is skipped for `null`. In 2.1, add a check that the repository is never called (`verifyNoInteractions(petRepository)`) when there is no number.
65	- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if derived `exists…` queries reject null arguments instead of matching `IS NULL`.
66	- **Confidence:** medium.
67	
68	**R4: AUTO-FIX+REVERIFY.** Where: task 4.1.
69	- **Claim:** Task 4.1 names only the add handler's regression test. The edit handler's `catch` also gets the microchip branch (design:72), but no task checks the constraint on the edit path, or its "other violation is rethrown" case.
70	- **Evidence:** tasks.md:33 says "`createOtherIntegrityViolationIsRethrown` still passes". `editOtherIntegrityViolationIsRethrown` exists at `PetControllerCharacterizationTests.java:454` and isn't mentioned.
71	- **Fix:** Run both scenarios against both handlers.
72	- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if "New PetControllerTests cases" is meant to cover both handlers and a check confirms it.
73	- **Confidence:** medium.
74	
75	**R5: INFORMATIONAL.** Where: design:106-107.
76	- **Claim:** The Postgres script can be re-run (`IF NOT EXISTS`); the MySQL one can't (`ADD COLUMN` with no guard). Running the MySQL script a second time fails loudly at its first statement and changes nothing, so the risk is low.
77	- **Evidence:** design:106 vs design:107.
78	- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if the MySQL script is meant to be re-runnable.
79	- **Confidence:** high.
80	
81	**R6: INFORMATIONAL.** Where: design:7, design:76; F11.
82	- **Claim:** The design's freeze-store claim, labelled "not re-run here", is now confirmed. Adding one `rejectValue` to a controller fails the build, and D19's route (no new controller call) keeps the frozen counts.
83	- **Evidence:**
84	  - The harness probe: control PASS; the probe run FAILs with "was violated (1 times)" at `PetController.java:127`.
85	  - VERIFIED: the store records the calls at lines 112, 132, 149 and 163, but the code has them at 111, 126, 143 and 157, and the control still passes. So matching ignores line numbers.
86	- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if the control run failed.
87	- **Confidence:** high.
88	
89	**R7: INFORMATIONAL.** Where: baseline `pets` Purpose.
90	- **Claim:** The baseline says it doesn't cover the GET forms, but the change adds a GET-form requirement. The change postpones the Purpose edit to archive time.
91	- **Evidence:** `openspec/specs/pets/spec.md:5`; tasks.md:48.
92	- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if OpenSpec deltas can modify Purpose.
93	- **Confidence:** high.
94	
95	**R8: INFORMATIONAL.** Where: design INFERRED claims.
96	- **Claim:** Each design claim labelled INFERRED has a task that checks it:
97	  - NULLs are allowed by a unique constraint: tasks 1.3 and 1.5.
98	  - Thymeleaf renders a null as an empty value: task 5.1.
99	  - The edited pet is detached, so the uniqueness query can't flush half-edited values: task 3.5. The risk is real: `editRejectedFormHasAlreadyBoundValuesOntoOwnersPet` (`PetControllerCharacterizationTests.java:406-416`) shows binding writes onto the loaded pet.
100	  - Postgres's `IF NOT EXISTS` finds the index the script made: task 1.5.
101	  - H2's error message names the constraint: task 1.4.
102	- **Caveat:** the MySQL and Postgres checks are skipped without Docker, as D23 records.
103	- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if any of those tasks can't observe the claim.
104	- **Confidence:** medium.
105	
106	The delta against the baseline is consistent. The two baseline requirements that the microchip number changes ("Duplicate names caught by the database", "Validation errors are reported together") are MODIFIED with all their scenarios kept. The other baseline requirements are not contradicted. Every requirement has a task with a check.
107	
108	## 3. For the person
109	
110	1. **R1: How should MySQL get from the old code to the new one, given that the old code can't restart on a migrated table?**
111	   - **Evidence:** `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48` inserts by position; `spring.sql.init.mode=always` (`application-mysql.properties:7`); design:114 and 119 rely on the old code working against the new table.
112	   - **Options:**
113	     - (a) **Two releases.** First ship only the column lists in `data.sql`, which work on the old table. Then run the migration, then ship the microchip number.
114	     - (b) **An `INVISIBLE` column.** Add the MySQL column as `INVISIBLE` (supported by the `mysql:9.7` image in `docker-compose.yml:3`). Positional inserts skip invisible columns, and Hibernate names its columns. This is INFERRED and should be checked by R2's test.
115	     - (c) **Accept the limit.** Accept that rollback on MySQL means editing the old `data.sql` too, and say so in D23.
116	   - **My recommendation:** (a) is the simplest and doesn't depend on MySQL features. Whichever you choose, D23 needs an amendment, because its stated reason ("never names the column") is wrong for MySQL.
117	
118	R2–R4 are mechanical once R1 is settled, and none of the findings is DISCUSS.
119

|---|---|---|
| D1 term | CARRIED | Proposal, design, spec and tasks avoid "chip number", "chip ID" and "transponder" (whole-word grep: only hits are in `decisions.md:7,9,34`, where D1 names the banned words and "chips" means the devices) |
| D2 optional | CARRIED | spec "Microchip number is optional"; task 2.1 |
| D3 15 digits, ISO only | CARRIED | spec "exactly 15 digits", scenario "A 10-character non-ISO number is rejected" |
| D4 unique across owners | CARRIED | spec "unique across all pets", scenario "A number held by another owner's pet" |
| D5 no lookup | CARRIED | proposal:5,19; design Non-Goals |
| D6 owner's page | CARRIED | `specs/owner-details/spec.md`; task 5.1 |
| D7 change number | CARRIED | spec "A pet's microchip number can be changed" |
| D8 empty clears, form shows stored | CARRIED | spec "Clearing…" and "The edit form shows the stored microchip number"; design 6 |
| D9 trim, remove spaces | CARRIED | spec "stored as its digits"; design 2 |
| D10 messages | CARRIED | design 3, design 4; spec scenarios |
| D11 no details of the other pet | CARRIED | spec "unique across all pets"; task 3.4 |
| D12 named constraint on 3 DBs | CARRIED | design 5 (on Postgres it is a unique index, as D23 allows) |
| D13 MySQL name constraint not fixed | CARRIED | design Non-Goals |
| D14 own number | CARRIED | spec "A pet keeps its own microchip number"; design 4 (two queries) |
| D15 no prefix check | CARRIED | design 3 |
| D16 empty value under the label | CARRIED | owner-details scenario "A pet without a microchip number" |
| D17 one error per field, reported with the others | CARRIED | spec "One microchip number error at a time"; MODIFIED "Validation errors are reported together" |
| D18 placement is a design call | CARRIED | design 4 |
| D19 validator method called from `catch` | CARRIED | design 5; tasks 4.1, 4.3 |
| D20 | Replaced by D23 | — |
| D21 H2 add/edit/clear test | CARRIED | task 3.5 |
| D22 accepted wrong-pet case | CARRIED | proposal:23; design Risks |
| D23 migration | CARRIED in text, but its premise is wrong on MySQL | design 8. D23 says "the old code keeps working against the new table because it never names the column". On MySQL that is false (R1). |
| D24 no visit form | CARRIED | design Non-Goals; tasks follow-up |

**Added scope:** none that isn't needed.
- The `owner-details` capability (D6), the message keys (the sync test requires them), the `data.sql` column lists (positional inserts) and the `testcontainers-postgresql` dependency (D23's tests) all follow from a decision or the code.
- The seed-insert fix is correct for new databases (VERIFIED: `db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48` insert by position; `db/postgres/data.sql:36-48` names its columns).

**Open section:** "None on PC-301's frontier". The follow-ups are listed in tasks.md (Workflow follow-up). The ticket raises no question that the log and the change leave unanswered: the "scanned" use is D5, "two pets" is D4, and there is no pet deletion (VERIFIED: grep for `delete|remove` in `owner/` finds nothing).

## 2. Findings

**R1: BLOCK.** Where: design Decision 8, "Rollback" step 1 and "Deployment" step 1; D23.
- **Claim:** On MySQL, the old code cannot start against a migrated `pets` table. The old `data.sql` inserts pets by position with 5 values, the migrated table has 6 columns, and init runs on every start with no `continue-on-error`. So "redeploy the old code" (rollback) fails, and so does any restart of old instances between step 1 and step 2. Postgres is not affected.
- **Evidence:**
  - VERIFIED: `db/mysql/data.sql:36` `INSERT IGNORE INTO pets VALUES (1, 'Leo', '2000-09-07', 1, 1);`
  - VERIFIED: `application-mysql.properties:7` `spring.sql.init.mode=always`. No `spring.sql.init.continue-on-error` in that file or in `application.properties`.
  - VERIFIED: design:114 says "The old code keeps working against the new table because it never names the column".
  - VERIFIED: Postgres's old `data.sql` names its columns (`db/postgres/data.sql:36`).
  - INFERRED, not run: MySQL raises error 1136, "Column count doesn't match value count", and `IGNORE` does not suppress it. That would make startup fail.
- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if MySQL 9.7 accepts a 5-value positional `INSERT IGNORE` into a 6-column table, or if something else sets `continue-on-error=true`.
- **Confidence:** medium-high.

**R2: AUTO-FIX+REVERIFY.** Where: task 1.5.
- **Claim:** The migration test runs the *new* `schema.sql` on the migrated database, but never the *old* `schema.sql` and `data.sql`. So nothing checks D23's "old code keeps working" claim, the very assumption R1 breaks.
- **Evidence:** tasks.md:11, "Finally it runs the new `schema.sql` against the migrated database". There is no step for the old scripts.
- **Fix:** After migrating, run the old commit's `schema.sql` and `data.sql` too, and assert they succeed.
- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if some other task runs the old init scripts against a migrated table.
- **Confidence:** high.

**R3: AUTO-FIX+REVERIFY.** Where: design Decision 4; task 2.1.
- **Claim:** The design doesn't say the uniqueness query is skipped when there is no number. A Spring Data derived `existsByMicrochipNumber(null)` turns into `IS NULL`, so it would find any pet without a number and reject a second pet without one as a duplicate.
- **Why tests could miss it:** Task 2.1's "no number accepted" uses a mocked repository, which returns `false` by default, so that test would pass with the bug. Indirect coverage exists: all seeded H2 pets have no number, so task 3.5's clear step and the existing `PetClinicConcurrencyTests` would probably fail. That coverage is accidental, not designed.
- **Evidence:**
  - VERIFIED: design:55 says "runs only when the format check passes". It doesn't say whether an absent number "passes".
  - INFERRED: Spring Data JPA turns a null argument into `IS NULL`.
- **Fix:** In design 4, state that the query is skipped for `null`. In 2.1, add a check that the repository is never called (`verifyNoInteractions(petRepository)`) when there is no number.
- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if derived `exists…` queries reject null arguments instead of matching `IS NULL`.
- **Confidence:** medium.

**R4: AUTO-FIX+REVERIFY.** Where: task 4.1.
- **Claim:** Task 4.1 names only the add handler's regression test. The edit handler's `catch` also gets the microchip branch (design:72), but no task checks the constraint on the edit path, or its "other violation is rethrown" case.
- **Evidence:** tasks.md:33 says "`createOtherIntegrityViolationIsRethrown` still passes". `editOtherIntegrityViolationIsRethrown` exists at `PetControllerCharacterizationTests.java:454` and isn't mentioned.
- **Fix:** Run both scenarios against both handlers.
- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if "New PetControllerTests cases" is meant to cover both handlers and a check confirms it.
- **Confidence:** medium.

**R5: INFORMATIONAL.** Where: design:106-107.
- **Claim:** The Postgres script can be re-run (`IF NOT EXISTS`); the MySQL one can't (`ADD COLUMN` with no guard). Running the MySQL script a second time fails loudly at its first statement and changes nothing, so the risk is low.
- **Evidence:** design:106 vs design:107.
- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if the MySQL script is meant to be re-runnable.
- **Confidence:** high.

**R6: INFORMATIONAL.** Where: design:7, design:76; F11.
- **Claim:** The design's freeze-store claim, labelled "not re-run here", is now confirmed. Adding one `rejectValue` to a controller fails the build, and D19's route (no new controller call) keeps the frozen counts.
- **Evidence:**
  - The harness probe: control PASS; the probe run FAILs with "was violated (1 times)" at `PetController.java:127`.
  - VERIFIED: the store records the calls at lines 112, 132, 149 and 163, but the code has them at 111, 126, 143 and 157, and the control still passes. So matching ignores line numbers.
- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if the control run failed.
- **Confidence:** high.

**R7: INFORMATIONAL.** Where: baseline `pets` Purpose.
- **Claim:** The baseline says it doesn't cover the GET forms, but the change adds a GET-form requirement. The change postpones the Purpose edit to archive time.
- **Evidence:** `openspec/specs/pets/spec.md:5`; tasks.md:48.
- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if OpenSpec deltas can modify Purpose.
- **Confidence:** high.

**R8: INFORMATIONAL.** Where: design INFERRED claims.
- **Claim:** Each design claim labelled INFERRED has a task that checks it:
  - NULLs are allowed by a unique constraint: tasks 1.3 and 1.5.
  - Thymeleaf renders a null as an empty value: task 5.1.
  - The edited pet is detached, so the uniqueness query can't flush half-edited values: task 3.5. The risk is real: `editRejectedFormHasAlreadyBoundValuesOntoOwnersPet` (`PetControllerCharacterizationTests.java:406-416`) shows binding writes onto the loaded pet.
  - Postgres's `IF NOT EXISTS` finds the index the script made: task 1.5.
  - H2's error message names the constraint: task 1.4.
- **Caveat:** the MySQL and Postgres checks are skipped without Docker, as D23 records.
- **Falsification:** This finding is wrong if any of those tasks can't observe the claim.
- **Confidence:** medium.

The delta against the baseline is consistent. The two baseline requirements that the microchip number changes ("Duplicate names caught by the database", "Validation errors are reported together") are MODIFIED with all their scenarios kept. The other baseline requirements are not contradicted. Every requirement has a task with a check.

## 3. For the person

1. **R1: How should MySQL get from the old code to the new one, given that the old code can't restart on a migrated table?**
   - **Evidence:** `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48` inserts by position; `spring.sql.init.mode=always` (`application-mysql.properties:7`); design:114 and 119 rely on the old code working against the new table.
   - **Options:**
     - (a) **Two releases.** First ship only the column lists in `data.sql`, which work on the old table. Then run the migration, then ship the microchip number.
     - (b) **An `INVISIBLE` column.** Add the MySQL column as `INVISIBLE` (supported by the `mysql:9.7` image in `docker-compose.yml:3`). Positional inserts skip invisible columns, and Hibernate names its columns. This is INFERRED and should be checked by R2's test.
     - (c) **Accept the limit.** Accept that rollback on MySQL means editing the old `data.sql` too, and say so in D23.
   - **My recommendation:** (a) is the simplest and doesn't depend on MySQL features. Whichever you choose, D23 needs an amendment, because its stated reason ("never names the column") is wrong for MySQL.

R2–R4 are mechanical once R1 is settled, and none of the findings is DISCUSS.

## What Changes

Dashes, dots and other characters are not removed. The country and manufacturer code is not checked (D3, D9, D10, D15).
- A microchip number is unique across all pets of all owners. A duplicate gets "is already in use" and nothing more: no other pet or owner is named (D4, D10, D11). A pet never conflicts with its own number (D14).

Not in this change: looking up a pet by its microchip number (D5), the microchip number on the visit form (D24), and the unnamed MySQL owner-and-pet-name constraint (D13, F4). The lookup ticket takes the visit form; the MySQL constraint needs its own ticket.

1	# Design
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	See `proposal.md` for the motivation, and `specs/pets/spec.md` and `specs/owner-details/spec.md` for the requirements. The facts below shape how the change is built. Each is labelled VERIFIED (code opened) or INFERRED (not checked).
6	
7	- **Validation placement.** `ArchitectureTests.java:36-43` forbids controllers from calling `Errors.rejectValue`, because field validation belongs in `PetValidator`. The rule is wrapped in `freeze(...)`, so the calls that already exist are recorded in `src/test/resources/archunit_store/1cbfc1d1-…` and tolerated. That includes the four calls in `PetController`'s two POST handlers. VERIFIED. The store counts calls per method, so one more `rejectValue` call in a POST handler fails the rule (F11, from the reviewers' probe; not re-run here).
8	- **Validator wiring.** `PetValidator` is created with `new PetValidator()` in `PetController.initPetBinder` (`PetController.java:95`). It has no repository (F6). VERIFIED.
9	- **Pet ids.** The `id` field cannot be bound from the form (`PetController.java:96`). On edit, the `pet` model attribute is the owner's pet loaded by the path's `petId` (`PetController.java:74-86`). So `pet.getId()` can be trusted when excluding a pet's own number. VERIFIED.
10	- **Edit copies fields.** `updatePetDetails` copies name, birth date and type onto the owner's pet (`PetController.java:177-191`). A new field is not copied unless it is added there. VERIFIED.
11	- **Database violations.** `isDuplicatePetNameViolation` matches the constraint name in the exception message, ignoring case (`PetController.java:193-196`). VERIFIED.
12	- **Schema setup.** The schema is created by `spring.sql.init` from `db/${database}/schema.sql`, and Hibernate does not manage the DDL (`application.properties:3,10`). The MySQL and Postgres scripts use `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` (`db/mysql/schema.sql:38`, `db/postgres/schema.sql:36`). VERIFIED.
13	- **Open session.** `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` (`application.properties:11`). VERIFIED.
14	- **Message files.** `I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkI18nPropertyFilesAreInSync` requires every key of `messages.properties` in every `messages_*.properties` except `messages_en` (`I18nPropertiesSyncTest.java:112-127`). VERIFIED.
15	
16	## Goals / Non-Goals
17	
18	**Goals:**
19	
20	- Put the format and uniqueness rules in `PetValidator`, so the add and edit forms share them and the architecture rule's intent holds.
21	- Make the database the final guard against duplicates, under one constraint name on all three databases.
22	
23	**Non-Goals:**
24	
25	- No index or query for finding a pet by its microchip number beyond what the uniqueness check needs (D5).
26	- No change to the owner-and-pet-name constraint on MySQL (D13).
27	- No schema migration tool. The project has none, so the migration scripts of Decision 8 are applied by hand (known gap, D23).
28	- No microchip number on the visit form (D24). It goes on the list for the lookup ticket (D5).
29	
30	## Decisions
31	
32	### 1. Storage: a nullable `microchip_number` column, with no number stored as NULL
33	
34	`pets.microchip_number` is `VARCHAR(15)` on H2 and MySQL and `TEXT` on Postgres, matching each script's existing style. It is nullable. "No microchip number" is stored as `NULL`, never as `''`. A unique constraint allows any number of NULLs on H2, MySQL and Postgres, but only one `''` (INFERRED from each database's documented behaviour). An empty string would therefore make the second pet without a number a duplicate (see the scenario "Two pets without a microchip number").
35	
36	*Alternative rejected:* `CHAR(15)`. It pads values, and the format check already fixes the length.
37	
38	### 2. Normalisation in `Pet.setMicrochipNumber`
39	
40	The setter trims the value and removes every `' '`. If the result is empty, it stores `null`. Other characters, including dashes, dots and inner tabs, are left in place for the validator to reject (D9). Putting this in the entity means that whatever path sets the value, the validator, the uniqueness query and the stored column all see the same normalised string.
41	
42	*Alternative rejected:* a `PropertyEditor` registered in `PetController.initPetBinder`. It works only for web binding, and validator tests would have to repeat the normalisation.
43	
44	### 3. Format check: `[0-9]{15}` in `PetValidator`
45	
46	The check uses `[0-9]` rather than `\d`, so that the rule cannot quietly widen to other digit characters if the pattern ever gets Unicode flags. The error code is `microchipNumber.invalid`, following the existing `telephone.invalid` (`messages.properties:34`), with the message "must be 15 digits". The prefix (country or manufacturer code) is not checked (D15).
47	
48	### 4. Uniqueness check in `PetValidator`, through a new `PetRepository`
49	
50	The new interface is `PetRepository extends Repository<Pet, Integer>`. It has only what the check needs:
51	
52	- `existsByMicrochipNumber(String)`, for a new pet, and
53	- `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot(String, Integer)`, for an existing pet (D14).
54	
55	Two methods are needed because `id <> NULL` is never true in SQL. A single `AndIdNot` query called with a null id would never find a duplicate on the add form. `PetValidator` gets a constructor that takes `PetRepository`, and `PetController` injects it and calls `new PetValidator(pets)` in `initPetBinder`. The uniqueness query runs only when the format check passes (D17), so the field gets at most one error. The error code is the existing `duplicate` ("is already in use", `messages.properties:4`), and the error carries no argument that names the other pet (D11).
56	
57	On edit, the bound `pet` is a detached entity (`open-in-view=false`), so the `exists` query cannot flush the half-edited pet first. INFERRED, and covered by the G3 test (D21, task 3.5), which runs on H2. Task 3 otherwise runs on mocked repositories and cannot show this.
58	
59	*Alternatives rejected:*
60	
61	- A check in the controller, as the pet-name check does today. It adds a `rejectValue` call that the frozen rule exists to stop.
62	- A query on `OwnerRepository`. That repository finds owners. A pet-level `exists` query does not belong there, and loading every owner to scan their pets would not scale.
63	
64	### 5. Database duplicates are rejected by a `PetValidator` method that the controller's `catch` calls
65	
66	The constraint is named `unique_pet_microchip_number` on all three databases:
67	
68	- H2: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD CONSTRAINT … UNIQUE`.
69	- MySQL: a named `CONSTRAINT … UNIQUE` inside `CREATE TABLE`.
70	- Postgres: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, as `unique_owner_pet_name` is (`db/postgres/schema.sql:45`).
71	
72	Neither constraint name is a substring of the other. Both POST handlers' `catch (DataIntegrityViolationException)` blocks check for the microchip constraint first, then the name constraint, then rethrow (spec: "Duplicate microchip numbers caught by the database", and the MODIFIED "Duplicate names caught by the database").
73	
74	The save fails after validation has run, so the validator's normal checks cannot see this case. Per D19, `PetValidator` gets a public method, for example `rejectDuplicateMicrochipNumber(Errors)`, that calls `rejectValue("microchipNumber", "duplicate")` with no argument naming another pet (D11). When the exception names `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case, the controller's `catch` calls this method and shows the form again. `PetController` builds one `PetValidator` from the injected `PetRepository`. It uses that validator both in `initPetBinder` and in the two `catch` blocks.
75	
76	No new `rejectValue` call is added to `PetController`. The four frozen calls of the name mapping (F10) stay as they are, and so does the freeze store. The implementer must not regenerate or edit the freeze store. If `ArchitectureTests` fails anyway, they stop and raise it with the ticket owner (task 4.3).
77	
78	*Alternatives rejected:*
79	
80	- One `rejectValue` call per `catch` that chooses the field from the error, `name` or `microchipNumber`. It reshapes the name mapping that the characterisation tests pin (D19).
81	- A waiver for two more frozen violations. It weakens the sensor (D19).
82	- `@ControllerAdvice`. It avoids the rule instead of meeting it (D19).
83	- New `rejectValue` calls in the controller, next to the name mapping. The probe shows that the freeze store rejects them (F11).
84	- Run the validator again after the failed save, so that the `exists` query finds the winning row. It depends on the other transaction's commit being visible and on the failed persistence context not flushing again. That is too fragile for a race-condition path.
85	
86	### 6. The edit copy includes the microchip number
87	
88	`updatePetDetails` also copies `microchipNumber`, including `null`, so that clearing the field removes the number (D8).
89	
90	### 7. Views and messages
91	
92	- Two new keys:
93	  - `microchipNumber=Microchip number` (glossary term, D1)
94	  - `microchipNumber.invalid=must be 15 digits`
95	
96	  Both go in `messages.properties` and every locale file except `messages_en`.
97	- `pets/createOrUpdatePetForm.html` gets a text input for `microchipNumber` through the existing `inputField` fragment, after the birth date. `th:field` fills it with the stored value on edit (spec: "The edit form shows the stored microchip number").
98	- `owners/ownerDetails.html` gets `<dt th:text="#{microchipNumber}">` and `<dd th:text="${pet.microchipNumber}">` after the type (`ownerDetails.html:55-56`). A `null` renders as an empty `dd` (INFERRED Thymeleaf behaviour), which is what D16 asks for.
99	
100	### 8. Existing MySQL and Postgres databases are migrated by one script each
101	
102	Per D23, which replaces D20. On an existing database, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pets` is skipped (`db/mysql/schema.sql:38`, `db/postgres/schema.sql:36`, VERIFIED), so the new column would never be created there. `spring.sql.init.mode=always` (`application-mysql.properties:7`, `application-postgres.properties:7`, VERIFIED) runs `schema.sql` on every start, so the new code would meet a table without the column (review R1; the exact failure is INFERRED, not run).
103	
104	The scripts:
105	
106	- `db/mysql/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD COLUMN microchip_number VARCHAR(15) NULL`, then `ALTER TABLE pets ADD CONSTRAINT unique_pet_microchip_number UNIQUE (microchip_number)`.
107	- `db/postgres/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS microchip_number TEXT`, then `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unique_pet_microchip_number ON pets (microchip_number)`, as `unique_owner_pet_name` is (`db/postgres/schema.sql:45`).
108	- None for H2: it is in memory and rebuilt on every start.
109	
110	Column types and the constraint name match Decisions 1 and 5. The scripts sit under `src/main/resources/db/<database>/` but are not run at start: `spring.sql.init` reads only `schema.sql` and `data.sql` there (`application.properties:3-4`, VERIFIED). The `schema.sql` files still create the column and the constraint for new databases (task 1.1). Each script starts with a comment that says to run it before deploying the new code.
111	
112	Deployment, in order:
113	
114	1. Run the script for the database against the existing database, while the old code is still running. The old code keeps working against the new table because it never names the column (D23).
115	2. Deploy the new code. Its `schema.sql` skips `CREATE TABLE`, and on Postgres the `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unique_pet_microchip_number` finds the index the script made (INFERRED; task 1.5 checks it).
116	
117	Rollback, in order:
118	
119	1. Redeploy the old code.
120	2. Leave the column and the constraint in place. Dropping them is a separate, later step, not part of this change.
121	
122	*Alternative rejected:* a migration tool such as Flyway or Liquibase. A real team would use one, but PetClinic has none (known gap, D23).
123	
124	## Risks / Trade-offs
125	
126	- [Existing MySQL or Postgres databases keep their old `pets` table, because `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` skips it] → The migration scripts of Decision 8 add the column and the constraint before the new code is deployed (D23). H2 is in memory and rebuilt on every start.
127	- [The new code is deployed before the migration script has run] → The steps in Decision 8 put the script first. Nothing in the app enforces the order, because PetClinic has no migration tool (known gap, D23).
128	- [The H2 and MySQL seed inserts give values by position (`db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`), so they would not match a sixth column] → Task 1.1 gives them a column list. No seeded pet gets a number (F8).
129	- [Each database words its duplicate-key message differently, and H2 may put the name in upper case inside a generated index name] → The match ignores case and looks for the constraint name as a substring. Task 1.4 checks the real message on H2: it saves two pets with the same number through `OwnerRepository.saveAndFlush`, so the validator does not run, and asserts that the `DataIntegrityViolationException` names `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case. The race test (task 4.2) does not check the real message. If one request commits before the other's `exists` query runs, the validator rejects the loser and the `catch` never runs, and the page looks the same either way. The `catch` itself is covered with mocked messages (task 4.1).
130	- **Known gap** (recorded with D20; D23 does not change it): the duplicate is not tested through the forms on MySQL or Postgres. Their integration tests run only with Docker (`MySqlIntegrationTests.java:43`, `PostgresIntegrationTests.java:67-68`), and they do not exercise the microchip constraint. This is left as it is.
131	- **Known gaps** (D23): PetClinic has no migration tool, so the scripts are applied by hand and nothing records whether a database has been migrated. The migration tests (task 1.5) run only with Docker; without it they are skipped, and must be reported as not run rather than as passed.
132	- [The validator now issues one query per submission that has a microchip number] → It is an indexed `exists` query on the unique constraint, so the cost is negligible.
133	- [Translations into nine languages may be poor] → The sync test checks only that the keys are present. Translations should be reviewed by a speaker before release, as for any new label.
134	- [A microchip number typed onto the wrong pet blocks the right pet, and reception cannot see which pet holds it] → Accepted until the lookup ticket (D22, following from D5 and D11).
135

- **Edit copies fields.** `updatePetDetails` copies name, birth date and type onto the owner's pet (`PetController.java:177-191`). A new field is not copied unless it is added there. VERIFIED.
- **Database violations.** `isDuplicatePetNameViolation` matches the constraint name in the exception message, ignoring case (`PetController.java:193-196`). VERIFIED.
- **Schema setup.** The schema is created by `spring.sql.init` from `db/${database}/schema.sql`, and Hibernate does not manage the DDL (`application.properties:3,10`). The MySQL and Postgres scripts use `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` (`db/mysql/schema.sql:38`, `db/postgres/schema.sql:36`). VERIFIED.
- **Open session.** `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` (`application.properties:11`). VERIFIED.
- **Message files.** `I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkI18nPropertyFilesAreInSync` requires every key of `messages.properties` in every `messages_*.properties` except `messages_en` (`I18nPropertiesSyncTest.java:112-127`). VERIFIED.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**

- Put the format and uniqueness rules in `PetValidator`, so the add and edit forms share them and the architecture rule's intent holds.
- Make the database the final guard against duplicates, under one constraint name on all three databases.

**Non-Goals:**

- No index or query for finding a pet by its microchip number beyond what the uniqueness check needs (D5).
- No change to the owner-and-pet-name constraint on MySQL (D13).
- No schema migration tool. The project has none, so the migration scripts of Decision 8 are applied by hand (known gap, D23).
- No microchip number on the visit form (D24). It goes on the list for the lookup ticket (D5).

## Decisions

### 1. Storage: a nullable `microchip_number` column, with no number stored as NULL

`pets.microchip_number` is `VARCHAR(15)` on H2 and MySQL and `TEXT` on Postgres, matching each script's existing style. It is nullable. "No microchip number" is stored as `NULL`, never as `''`. A unique constraint allows any number of NULLs on H2, MySQL and Postgres, but only one `''` (INFERRED from each database's documented behaviour). An empty string would therefore make the second pet without a number a duplicate (see the scenario "Two pets without a microchip number").

*Alternative rejected:* `CHAR(15)`. It pads values, and the format check already fixes the length.

### 2. Normalisation in `Pet.setMicrochipNumber`

The setter trims the value and removes every `' '`. If the result is empty, it stores `null`. Other characters, including dashes, dots and inner tabs, are left in place for the validator to reject (D9). Putting this in the entity means that whatever path sets the value, the validator, the uniqueness query and the stored column all see the same normalised string.

*Alternative rejected:* a `PropertyEditor` registered in `PetController.initPetBinder`. It works only for web binding, and validator tests would have to repeat the normalisation.

### 3. Format check: `[0-9]{15}` in `PetValidator`

The check uses `[0-9]` rather than `\d`, so that the rule cannot quietly widen to other digit characters if the pattern ever gets Unicode flags. The error code is `microchipNumber.invalid`, following the existing `telephone.invalid` (`messages.properties:34`), with the message "must be 15 digits". The prefix (country or manufacturer code) is not checked (D15).

### 4. Uniqueness check in `PetValidator`, through a new `PetRepository`

The new interface is `PetRepository extends Repository<Pet, Integer>`. It has only what the check needs:

- `existsByMicrochipNumber(String)`, for a new pet, and
- `existsByMicrochipNumberAndIdNot(String, Integer)`, for an existing pet (D14).

Two methods are needed because `id <> NULL` is never true in SQL. A single `AndIdNot` query called with a null id would never find a duplicate on the add form. `PetValidator` gets a constructor that takes `PetRepository`, and `PetController` injects it and calls `new PetValidator(pets)` in `initPetBinder`. The uniqueness query runs only when the format check passes (D17), so the field gets at most one error. The error code is the existing `duplicate` ("is already in use", `messages.properties:4`), and the error carries no argument that names the other pet (D11).

On edit, the bound `pet` is a detached entity (`open-in-view=false`), so the `exists` query cannot flush the half-edited pet first. INFERRED, and covered by the G3 test (D21, task 3.5), which runs on H2. Task 3 otherwise runs on mocked repositories and cannot show this.

*Alternatives rejected:*

- A check in the controller, as the pet-name check does today. It adds a `rejectValue` call that the frozen rule exists to stop.
- A query on `OwnerRepository`. That repository finds owners. A pet-level `exists` query does not belong there, and loading every owner to scan their pets would not scale.

### 5. Database duplicates are rejected by a `PetValidator` method that the controller's `catch` calls

The constraint is named `unique_pet_microchip_number` on all three databases:

- H2: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD CONSTRAINT … UNIQUE`.
- MySQL: a named `CONSTRAINT … UNIQUE` inside `CREATE TABLE`.
- Postgres: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, as `unique_owner_pet_name` is (`db/postgres/schema.sql:45`).

Neither constraint name is a substring of the other. Both POST handlers' `catch (DataIntegrityViolationException)` blocks check for the microchip constraint first, then the name constraint, then rethrow (spec: "Duplicate microchip numbers caught by the database", and the MODIFIED "Duplicate names caught by the database").

The save fails after validation has run, so the validator's normal checks cannot see this case. Per D19, `PetValidator` gets a public method, for example `rejectDuplicateMicrochipNumber(Errors)`, that calls `rejectValue("microchipNumber", "duplicate")` with no argument naming another pet (D11). When the exception names `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case, the controller's `catch` calls this method and shows the form again. `PetController` builds one `PetValidator` from the injected `PetRepository`. It uses that validator both in `initPetBinder` and in the two `catch` blocks.

No new `rejectValue` call is added to `PetController`. The four frozen calls of the name mapping (F10) stay as they are, and so does the freeze store. The implementer must not regenerate or edit the freeze store. If `ArchitectureTests` fails anyway, they stop and raise it with the ticket owner (task 4.3).

*Alternatives rejected:*

- One `rejectValue` call per `catch` that chooses the field from the error, `name` or `microchipNumber`. It reshapes the name mapping that the characterisation tests pin (D19).
- A waiver for two more frozen violations. It weakens the sensor (D19).
- `@ControllerAdvice`. It avoids the rule instead of meeting it (D19).
- New `rejectValue` calls in the controller, next to the name mapping. The probe shows that the freeze store rejects them (F11).
- Run the validator again after the failed save, so that the `exists` query finds the winning row. It depends on the other transaction's commit being visible and on the failed persistence context not flushing again. That is too fragile for a race-condition path.

### 6. The edit copy includes the microchip number

`updatePetDetails` also copies `microchipNumber`, including `null`, so that clearing the field removes the number (D8).

### 7. Views and messages

- Two new keys:
  - `microchipNumber=Microchip number` (glossary term, D1)
  - `microchipNumber.invalid=must be 15 digits`

  Both go in `messages.properties` and every locale file except `messages_en`.
- `pets/createOrUpdatePetForm.html` gets a text input for `microchipNumber` through the existing `inputField` fragment, after the birth date. `th:field` fills it with the stored value on edit (spec: "The edit form shows the stored microchip number").
- `owners/ownerDetails.html` gets `<dt th:text="#{microchipNumber}">` and `<dd th:text="${pet.microchipNumber}">` after the type (`ownerDetails.html:55-56`). A `null` renders as an empty `dd` (INFERRED Thymeleaf behaviour), which is what D16 asks for.

### 8. Existing MySQL and Postgres databases are migrated by one script each

Per D23, which replaces D20. On an existing database, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pets` is skipped (`db/mysql/schema.sql:38`, `db/postgres/schema.sql:36`, VERIFIED), so the new column would never be created there. `spring.sql.init.mode=always` (`application-mysql.properties:7`, `application-postgres.properties:7`, VERIFIED) runs `schema.sql` on every start, so the new code would meet a table without the column (review R1; the exact failure is INFERRED, not run).

The scripts:

- `db/mysql/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD COLUMN microchip_number VARCHAR(15) NULL`, then `ALTER TABLE pets ADD CONSTRAINT unique_pet_microchip_number UNIQUE (microchip_number)`.
- `db/postgres/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS microchip_number TEXT`, then `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unique_pet_microchip_number ON pets (microchip_number)`, as `unique_owner_pet_name` is (`db/postgres/schema.sql:45`).
- None for H2: it is in memory and rebuilt on every start.

Column types and the constraint name match Decisions 1 and 5. The scripts sit under `src/main/resources/db/<database>/` but are not run at start: `spring.sql.init` reads only `schema.sql` and `data.sql` there (`application.properties:3-4`, VERIFIED). The `schema.sql` files still create the column and the constraint for new databases (task 1.1). Each script starts with a comment that says to run it before deploying the new code.

Deployment, in order:

1. Run the script for the database against the existing database, while the old code is still running. The old code keeps working against the new table because it never names the column (D23).
2. Deploy the new code. Its `schema.sql` skips `CREATE TABLE`, and on Postgres the `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unique_pet_microchip_number` finds the index the script made (INFERRED; task 1.5 checks it).

Rollback, in order:

1. Redeploy the old code.
2. Leave the column and the constraint in place. Dropping them is a separate, later step, not part of this change.

*Alternative rejected:* a migration tool such as Flyway or Liquibase. A real team would use one, but PetClinic has none (known gap, D23).

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Existing MySQL or Postgres databases keep their old `pets` table, because `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` skips it] → The migration scripts of Decision 8 add the column and the constraint before the new code is deployed (D23). H2 is in memory and rebuilt on every start.
- [The new code is deployed before the migration script has run] → The steps in Decision 8 put the script first. Nothing in the app enforces the order, because PetClinic has no migration tool (known gap, D23).
- [The H2 and MySQL seed inserts give values by position (`db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`), so they would not match a sixth column] → Task 1.1 gives them a column list. No seeded pet gets a number (F8).
- [Each database words its duplicate-key message differently, and H2 may put the name in upper case inside a generated index name] → The match ignores case and looks for the constraint name as a substring. Task 1.4 checks the real message on H2: it saves two pets with the same number through `OwnerRepository.saveAndFlush`, so the validator does not run, and asserts that the `DataIntegrityViolationException` names `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case. The race test (task 4.2) does not check the real message. If one request commits before the other's `exists` query runs, the validator rejects the loser and the `catch` never runs, and the page looks the same either way. The `catch` itself is covered with mocked messages (task 4.1).
- **Known gap** (recorded with D20; D23 does not change it): the duplicate is not tested through the forms on MySQL or Postgres. Their integration tests run only with Docker (`MySqlIntegrationTests.java:43`, `PostgresIntegrationTests.java:67-68`), and they do not exercise the microchip constraint. This is left as it is.
- **Known gaps** (D23): PetClinic has no migration tool, so the scripts are applied by hand and nothing records whether a database has been migrated. The migration tests (task 1.5) run only with Docker; without it they are skipped, and must be reported as not run rather than as passed.
- [The validator now issues one query per submission that has a microchip number] → It is an indexed `exists` query on the unique constraint, so the cost is negligible.
- [Translations into nine languages may be poor] → The sync test checks only that the keys are present. Translations should be reviewed by a speaker before release, as for any new label.
- [A microchip number typed onto the wrong pet blocks the right pet, and reception cannot see which pet holds it] → Accepted until the lookup ticket (D22, following from D5 and D11).

# Spec Delta

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Microchip number is optional

The system SHALL accept a pet without a microchip number on both the add form and the edit form. An empty or blank microchip number SHALL be stored as no microchip number.

#### Scenario: A pet is added without a microchip number

- **WHEN** the add form is submitted with an empty microchip number and a valid name, type and birth date
- **THEN** the pet is saved with no microchip number
- **AND** the browser is redirected to the owner's page with the message "New Pet has been Added"

#### Scenario: A blank microchip number counts as none

- **WHEN** the add form is submitted with the microchip number "   " and otherwise valid values
- **THEN** the pet is saved with no microchip number

#### Scenario: Two pets without a microchip number

- **WHEN** a pet with no microchip number exists and another pet is added without a microchip number
- **THEN** the second pet is saved

### Requirement: Microchip number is stored as its digits

Before checking a microchip number, the system SHALL trim the entered value and remove every space from it. The system SHALL store only the resulting digits, and SHALL NOT remove any other character.

#### Scenario: Spaces are removed

- **WHEN** the add form is submitted with the microchip number " 985 141 000 123 456 " and otherwise valid values
- **THEN** the pet is saved with the microchip number "985141000123456"

#### Scenario: Dashes are not removed

- **WHEN** the add form is submitted with the microchip number "985-141-000-123-456"
- **THEN** the form is shown again with "must be 15 digits" on the microchip number
- **AND** nothing is saved

### Requirement: Microchip number is exactly 15 digits

The system MUST reject, on either form, a microchip number that is not exactly 15 digits after its spaces are removed, with the error "must be 15 digits" on the microchip number. The system SHALL NOT check the country or manufacturer code in the first three digits.

#### Scenario: Fifteen digits are accepted

- **WHEN** either form is submitted with the microchip number "985141000123456" and otherwise valid values
- **THEN** the pet is saved with that microchip number

#### Scenario: Any first three digits are accepted

- **WHEN** either form is submitted with the microchip number "000000000000001" and otherwise valid values
- **THEN** the pet is saved with that microchip number

#### Scenario: Fourteen digits are rejected

- **WHEN** either form is submitted with the microchip number "98514100012345"
- **THEN** the form is shown again with "must be 15 digits" on the microchip number
- **AND** nothing is saved

#### Scenario: Sixteen digits are rejected

- **WHEN** either form is submitted with the microchip number "9851410001234567"
- **THEN** the form is shown again with "must be 15 digits" on the microchip number
- **AND** nothing is saved

#### Scenario: A 10-character non-ISO number is rejected

- **WHEN** the add form is submitted with the microchip number "0A0139F53B"
- **THEN** the form is shown again with "must be 15 digits" on the microchip number
- **AND** nothing is saved

### Requirement: Microchip number is unique across all pets

The system MUST reject a microchip number that another pet already has, whichever owner that pet belongs to, with the error "is already in use" on the microchip number. The error SHALL NOT name or show the other pet, its owner or any of their details.

#### Scenario: A number held by another owner's pet

- **WHEN** a pet of owner A has the microchip number "985141000123456" and the add form for owner B is submitted with " 985141000123456"
- **THEN** the form is shown again with "is already in use" on the microchip number
- **AND** nothing is saved
- **AND** the page shows neither the other pet's name nor owner A's name

#### Scenario: Editing a pet to another pet's number

- **WHEN** the owner has pets "petty" and "doggy", "petty" has the microchip number "985141000123456", and "doggy" is edited to the microchip number "985 141 000 123 456"
- **THEN** the form is shown again with "is already in use" on the microchip number
- **AND** nothing is saved

### Requirement: A pet keeps its own microchip number

The system SHALL NOT report a pet's own microchip number as a duplicate, compared after spaces are removed. Saving a pet again with the number it already has SHALL be accepted.

#### Scenario: Saving a pet with its own number

- **WHEN** the pet "petty" has the microchip number "985141000123456" and its edit form is submitted with "985 141 000 123 456" and otherwise valid values
- **THEN** the edit is saved
- **AND** "petty" still has the microchip number "985141000123456"

### Requirement: A pet's microchip number can be changed

The system SHALL let the edit form replace a pet's stored microchip number with another one. The new number SHALL be checked by the same rules as on the add form.

#### Scenario: A new number replaces the stored one

- **WHEN** the pet "petty" has the microchip number "985141000123456" and its edit form is submitted with "985141000654321" and otherwise valid values
- **THEN** "petty" has the microchip number "985141000654321"

#### Scenario: A malformed new number is rejected

- **WHEN** the pet "petty" has the microchip number "985141000123456" and its edit form is submitted with "12345"
- **THEN** the form is shown again with "must be 15 digits" on the microchip number
- **AND** "petty" still has the microchip number "985141000123456" in the database

### Requirement: Clearing the microchip number on the edit form removes it

The system SHALL remove a pet's stored microchip number when the edit form is submitted with an empty or blank microchip number.

#### Scenario: The field is cleared

- **WHEN** the pet "petty" has the microchip number "985141000123456" and its edit form is submitted with an empty microchip number and otherwise valid values
- **THEN** the edit is saved
- **AND** "petty" has no microchip number

### Requirement: The edit form shows the stored microchip number

The system SHALL fill the microchip number field of the edit form with the pet's stored microchip number, so that an empty field on submission is a deliberate choice. A pet without a microchip number SHALL show an empty field.

#### Scenario: A pet with a number

- **WHEN** the edit form is opened for a pet with the microchip number "985141000123456"
- **THEN** the microchip number field holds "985141000123456"

#### Scenario: A pet without a number

- **WHEN** the edit form is opened for a pet without a microchip number
- **THEN** the microchip number field is empty

### Requirement: One microchip number error at a time

The system SHALL report at most one error on the microchip number. A malformed number SHALL get "must be 15 digits" only, and a well-formed duplicate SHALL get "is already in use" only.

#### Scenario: A malformed number is not checked for duplicates

- **WHEN** a pet has the microchip number "985141000123456" and the add form is submitted with "985141000123456-"
- **THEN** the form is shown again with exactly one error on the microchip number, "must be 15 digits"

#### Scenario: A duplicate gets only the duplicate error

- **WHEN** a pet has the microchip number "985141000123456" and the add form for another owner is submitted with "985141000123456"
- **THEN** the form is shown again with exactly one error on the microchip number, "is already in use"

### Requirement: Duplicate microchip numbers caught by the database

When the database rejects a save because of the unique constraint on the microchip number, the system SHALL show the form again with "is already in use" on the microchip number. The constraint SHALL have the same name on H2, MySQL and Postgres.

#### Scenario: Two simultaneous adds with the same number

- **WHEN** two add requests, for different owners, with the same new microchip number arrive at the same time
- **THEN** exactly one pet with that microchip number is saved
- **AND** the other request adds no pet
- **AND** the other request gets the form again with "is already in use" on the microchip number

#### Scenario: The constraint is reported as a duplicate microchip number

- **WHEN** saving the owner fails with a data integrity violation whose message names the microchip number constraint, in any case
- **THEN** the form is shown again with "is already in use" on the microchip number
- **AND** the form does not show a duplicate-name error

#### Scenario: The name constraint is still reported on the name

- **WHEN** saving the owner fails with a data integrity violation whose message names `unique_owner_pet_name`
- **THEN** the form is shown again with "is already in use" on the name
- **AND** the form does not show an error on the microchip number

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Duplicate names caught by the database

When the database rejects a save because of the unique constraint on owner and pet name, the system SHALL show the form again with "is already in use" on the name. The system MUST NOT report any other data integrity violation as a duplicate name. A violation of the unique constraint on the microchip number is handled by the requirement "Duplicate microchip numbers caught by the database".

#### Scenario: Two simultaneous adds with the same name

- **WHEN** two add requests for the same owner and the same new name arrive at the same time
- **THEN** exactly one pet with that name is saved
- **AND** the other request adds no pet

#### Scenario: The constraint is reported as a duplicate name

- **WHEN** saving the owner fails with a data integrity violation whose message names `unique_owner_pet_name`, in any case
- **THEN** the form is shown again with "is already in use" on the name

#### Scenario: Another integrity violation

- **WHEN** saving the owner fails with a data integrity violation that names neither the owner-and-pet-name constraint nor the microchip number constraint
- **THEN** the request fails with that error
- **AND** the form does not show a duplicate-name error
- **AND** the form does not show an error on the microchip number

### Requirement: Validation errors are reported together

The system SHALL report every validation error of a submission at once, in no particular order, including an error on the microchip number, and SHALL NOT save the pet while any error remains.

#### Scenario: Three errors on the add form

- **WHEN** the add form is submitted with no type, the name of an existing pet and tomorrow's date
- **THEN** the form is shown again with three errors: "is required" on the type, "is already in use" on the name and "invalid date" on the birth date

#### Scenario: Two errors on the edit form

- **WHEN** a pet with no stored birth date is edited to the name of another pet, without a birth date
- **THEN** the form is shown again with two errors: "is required" on the birth date and "is already in use" on the name

#### Scenario: Three errors on the add form, one on the microchip number

- **WHEN** the add form is submitted with a valid type, the name of an existing pet of the owner, tomorrow's date and the microchip number "123"
- **THEN** the form is shown again with three errors: "is already in use" on the name, "invalid date" on the birth date and "must be 15 digits" on the microchip number

#### Scenario: Two errors on the edit form, one on the microchip number

- **WHEN** a pet is edited with an empty birth date and the microchip number of another owner's pet
